name: Yamuna Yatra
line: Twelve days and a thousand kilometres, downstream, from the source to Agra.
deck: From where it originates and is pristine, down to the point where it reaches Agra and is almost a toxic body of water. Twelve days. The river makes the argument. We only walk beside it.

figures.label: Youth leaders who have walked it

aims.h: Go the way the river goes
aims.p: In order, from the top, at walking pace. The objective is that the middle cannot be left out, and the middle is the part that makes the case.

aims.h: Run it often enough to be a record
aims.p: Thirty-odd repetitions of the same route is what makes this evidence rather than an expedition. One walk is an anecdote.
What we are aiming at is a school that builds a graded year around it, because a curriculum outlives whoever argued for it.
Most arguments about this river are conducted about one stretch of it. The intent is people who have stood at both ends and can say so.

how.p: The Yatra goes the river's way — downstream, Himalaya to plain. Nothing is flown over and nothing is skipped, so the change in the water happens in front of you instead of on a slide.

how.h: It has been run more than thirty times
how.p: Since 2004: the same twelve days, the same direction, a different set of young people each time. That repetition is the method. One river, described by three thousand people who have seen all of it.

how.h: For one school it is coursework
how.p: Vasant Valley School made the Yatra part of its Grade XI annual curriculum. That changes what the twelve days are — there is reading before it and work after it, and a student cannot opt out of the argument by enjoying the trip.

how.h: It is run with schools and with embassies
how.p: Schools bring the cohort. The American Embassy, the British Council and the European Union have stood behind it. Both halves are named further down, because on this page the names are the record.

who.p: Over three thousand of them have walked it since 2004. Twelve days is long, and the programme is built for people who will use it afterwards.

who.h: Schools that will build a year around it
who.p: Three schools are named further down this page as having sent cohorts, and one of them put the Yatra inside a graded year, with reading before it and work after.

who.h: Anybody who has only met the Delhi stretch
who.p: The river is pristine where it starts. Almost everybody who holds an opinion about the Yamuna has only seen the part that runs past a city.

done.p: Over thirty Yatras since 2004, and more than three thousand youth leaders down the whole thousand kilometres.
A school putting the Yatra inside its Grade XI year is the strongest outcome the programme has, because a curriculum outlives the people who argued for it.

holes.what: The stops between Yamunotri and Agra are not published here. We know both ends and the distance; the ten-stop route on our own older draft appears in no document we can check.
holes.unlocks: Confirmation of the ten stops (content ledger hole 12) would let this page draw the route it is named after.

holes.what: Twelve days of river and not one measurement of it taken by the people who walked it.
holes.unlocks: Any water readings the cohorts took would let this page put the river's own numbers beside the walk.

statement.under: Pristine at Yamunotri, almost a toxic body of water by Agra. Twelve days is how long that sentence takes to land, and we only walk beside it.
